lib_test.sh: drain_runner_vm: persistent poll failure retries then gives up at cap
lib_test.sh: drain_runner_vm: transient poll failure retries instead of proceeding immediately

items.statement: Deleting a fleet VM (RUNNER_TOKEN mode or no proj/vm match) succeeds without GL_TOKEN and does not touch the shared fleet runner.
tests: lib_test.sh: delete-gcp-vm.sh: neither RUNNER_TOKEN nor GL_TOKEN fails closed
lib_test.sh: delete-openshift-vm.sh: neither RUNNER_TOKEN nor GL_TOKEN fails closed

items.statement: delete-*-vm.sh drains the VM before deletion; --no-drain skips it.
create-*-vm.sh --recreate drains, deletes and recreates an existing VM using only create's env in fleet mode; absent the flag, refuse-on-existing is unchanged.
Recreating a fleet VM leaves the shared runner ID stable and does not cut a job that finishes within the drain cap.
Usage comments in create-*/delete-* describe capabilities, flags, modes and required credentials.

items.description: AC4 is neither implemented nor tested. The PR body says 'Closes #7257', but no create-gcp-vm.sh or create-openshift-vm.sh change is in the diff, so --recreate (drain -> delete -> create in one credential-consistent command) does not exist.
items.remediation: Add --recreate to both create scripts with lib_test.sh coverage (flag parsed, refuse-on-existing preserved without the flag), or downgrade the PR link to 'Refs #7257' and keep the issue open.
items.evidence: pr.json files[] contains only README.md, delete-gcp-vm.sh, delete-openshift-vm.sh, lib.sh, lib_test.sh.

items.description: The new --no-drain escape hatch has no test. The argument loop in both delete scripts partitions $@ into --no-drain vs vm_names, and nothing asserts the flag is stripped from the VM list or that the 'skipping drain (--no-drain)' branch is taken. A regression treating --no-drain as a VM name would pass CI.
items.remediation: Add to lib_test.sh: assert_fails_with 'delete-gcp-vm.sh: --no-drain is not a VM name' 'specify at least one VM name' with_clean_env GCP_PROJECT=p RUNNER_TOKEN=glrt-x bash "${DELETE_GCP}" --no-drain, plus the OpenShift twin. Runs offline with no gcloud/virtctl.
items.evidence: diff.patch adds the vm_names/--no-drain loop to both delete scripts; lib_test.sh adds no assertion mentioning --no-drain.

items.description: AC5 (recreating a fleet VM leaves the shared runner ID stable and does not cut a job that finishes within the drain cap) has no verification of any kind: no unit test, no e2e, and no documented manual verification step in the README change.
items.remediation: Add a manual verification note to hack/gitlab-runner-vm/README.md (drain a VM with a live job, confirm the shared runner ID is unchanged and the job completes), or file a follow-up issue for an e2e check.
items.evidence: No test or README section in the diff references runner ID stability or in-flight job completion.

items.description: AC2 is only tested in the negative. Both new delete-script tests assert that neither token fails closed; nothing asserts the positive path the AC states -- with RUNNER_TOKEN set and no GL_TOKEN, validation passes and deregistration is skipped. The lookup_runners=false branch and the 'skipping GitLab deregistration (fleet mode)' output are unexercised.
items.remediation: Add a test running with_clean_env GCP_PROJECT=p RUNNER_TOKEN=glrt-x bash "${DELETE_GCP}" fullsend-gitlab-runner-01 and assert the output does NOT contain 'GL_TOKEN is required' (a later failure on missing gcloud is fine).
items.evidence: lib_test.sh '== delete script validation ==' contains only the two assert_fails_with cases.

items.description: The two caveats the issue explicitly said the implementation must not get wrong are the two the tests do not pin: that the drain uses SIGQUIT rather than a bare systemctl stop (which trips Fedora's 45s TimeoutStopUSec abort), and that the unit is runtime-masked so Restart=always cannot restart the runner mid-drain. drain_capture_mock already captures the remote command string, so both are one grep away.
items.remediation: Extend the drain_capture_mock block in lib_test.sh to assert the captured command contains '-s QUIT' and 'systemctl mask --runtime gitlab-runner.service', and contains no bare 'systemctl stop gitlab-runner'.
items.evidence: The capture assertions check only 'sudo -u fedora podman ps', 'sudo -u fedora test -f' and 'sudo -u fedora sed -i'; the static regression greps pin shutdown_timeout, is-active and chown/chmod but never the signal or the mask.

items.description: --help in both delete scripts was rewritten from 'head -26 | tail -24' to an awk header scan, and neither rewritten path has a test -- while lib_test.sh already contains exactly this smoke test for create-gcp-vm.sh --help and create-openshift-vm.sh --help. An awk guard that silently prints nothing after a header edit would not fail CI.
items.remediation: Add assert_succeeds_with 'delete-gcp-vm.sh --help lists modes' '--no-drain' with_clean_env bash "${DELETE_GCP}" --help, plus the OpenShift twin, mirroring the existing create-script assertions.
items.evidence: diff.patch replaces the head/tail help extraction with awk in both delete scripts; no --help assertion for DELETE_GCP/DELETE_OCP is added.

items.description: No drain test covers the ordinary busy-to-idle transition. Every mock is always-idle, always-busy, always-failing, or service-active with an empty container list; none returns a runner-* container on one poll and idle on the next, which is the normal successful drain.
items.remediation: Add a counter mock that prints 'runner-abc123' on poll 1 and '__SVC__inactive' on poll 2, asserting 'OK: runner idle' appears and 'drain cap' does not.

items.description: Four of the new checks are source-text greps against lib.sh and the delete scripts (export vm_name..., 1i shutdown_timeout, sudo chown $cfg_owner, systemctl is-active). They assert a string exists, not that the behavior happens, so they pass on dead or unreachable code and break on harmless refactors; two of them duplicate assertions drain_capture_mock already makes behaviorally.
items.remediation: Keep the greps that have no behavioral equivalent and drop the two already covered behaviorally by drain_capture_mock, so implementation text is not pinned twice.
